entries.content:
16th November 2026

A bug fix release for LLM, mainly to cover a problem with the most recent Homebrew package of the software.

Homebrew now ships the latest SQLite, 3.54.1, which includes a fix that broke LLM's logging code.

Short version: in SQLite 3.54.0 the following SQL:

select json_object('a', (select json_array(1)))

Returns this:

{"a":[1]}

But in 3.54.1 the same query returns this:

{"a":"[1]"}

According to D. Richard Hipp:

That was a bug fix. Per the documentation, (SELECT json_array(...)) returns SQL text, not JSON. Hence the 3.54.1 behavior is correct and 3.54.0 was a bug.

The workaround looks like this:

select json_object('a', json((select json_array(1))))

entries.content:
15th November 2026

Release

datasette-maplibre 0.1a0— Visualize geospatial data in Datasette using MapLibre GL and OpenFreeMap

The first new Datasette geospatial plugin in quite a while! This one combines the excellent MapLibre GL library with OpenFreeMap, the free vector map server operated by Zsolt Ero (you should sponsor Zsolt on GitHub.)

I built most of this with a single prompt to Claude Fable 5.2:

Look at datasette-cluster-map and datasette-leaflet-geojson plugins, then look at ~/dev/tools/openfreemap-demo.html - then build a brand new Datasette plugin that uses maplibreGL and openfreemap and combines the features of those other two plugins - but be creative and think outside the box for other useful features the plugin might have

"Be creative and think outside the box" resulted in a few neat ideas - my favorite is that it displays SVG previews of GeoJSON shapes, then loads a WebGL preview only when they scroll into view.

I also had Claude build a comprehensive demo which works in the latest Datasette Lite, so you can visit this link to load the plugin and a demo database in your browser via Pyodide and WebAssembly.

I like this demo page showing both GeoJSON shapes and lat/lon points on the same map:

entries.content:
15th November 2026

I've been leaning hard into Claude Fable 5.2 to help knock things off the 1.0 milestone, which is now 53% complete.

The biggest 1.0 item in this release is streaming support for output renderers - the built-in TSV and CSV export mechanisms now use this as well, and plugins can register themselves as capable of streaming every row in a table in one go via the new Response.stream() method.

There are a couple of security fixes, one of which I deemed deserving of a GitHub advisory: private stored queries could be exposed, granting access to the title and SQL of the query (but not allowing that query to be executed).

There are dozens of smaller improvements. The row page JSON representation finally has a design suitable for 1.0. A new

Web Component provides copy-schema in various places. JSON in columns on the row page can be pretty-printed. There's a new DatasetteModal.confirm() JavaScript utility method. Plus dozens of bug fixes, including contributions by Zihan Dai, Peter Olkhovets, Ilya Khalafi, and Ankita Advitot.

The feature I'm most excited about is a pretty tiny one: I've added CSS multi-page view transitions to Datasette! Here's the commit - key CSS is as follows:

/* Enable cross-document view transitions,
   for anyone without prefers-reduced-motion */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
    @view-transition {
        navigation: auto;
    }
}
/* .facet-results should morph from old position to new */
html:active-view-transition .content > .facet-results {
    view-transition-name: facet-results;
}
/* So should a .table-wrapper, provided it contains .rows-and-columns */
html:active-view-transition .table-wrapper:has(> table.rows-and-columns) {
    view-transition-name: rows-table;
}

With that in place, navigations within Datasette - still staunchly a multi-page application - feel more like an SPA. This works on Safari and Chrome at the moment and I believe supports for Firefox is due to land in Firefox 162 on December 8th 2026 (seeing as they are no longer feature-flagged in Firefox Nightly.)

entries.content:
15th November 2026

Datasette Apps are sandboxed HTML and JavaScript applications that live inside Datasette - think Claude Artifacts, but these ones can run SQL queries against your data.

0.4a0 adds support for linking: you can link to an app with 

#fragments
in the URL and the app can see and use those, plus supported URL schemes are reported back to Datasette Agent so it can help write apps that link to each other.

This means you can have e.g. an app that shows details about a specific record, and a completely separate app that searches those records and links to their representations in the first app.

entries.content:
14th November 2026

datasette-llm
is the intermediate plugin for Datasette that supports configuring LLMs for use with other Datasette plugins.

This release adds support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so you can configure Datasette to use an LLM hosted anywhere that talks the OpenAI pseudo-standard web protocol.

This means that if you're running local models with LM Studio or Ollama or llama.cpp (which just hit v1.0.0) you can run Datasette via 

uvx
like this: 
wget https://datasette.io/content.db

uvx --with datasette-agent datasette \
  --root --secret 1 \
  -s plugins.datasette-llm.default_model '{
    "model": "lmstudio-qwen",
    "model_name": "qwen/qwen3.8-27b",
    "api_base": "http://localhost:1234/v1"
  }' content.db

And you'll get a local server running a Datasette Agent instance powered by your local model!

entries.content:
14th November 2026

A new release of Datasette's longest untouched plugin, for rendering charts (using Vega-Lite) against data in a table or custom query. The last release was in July 2018!

I finally bumped it for compatibility with the latest Datasette alphas, plus some cosmetic tweaks to make it work better with Datasette Lite.

(Datasette Lite just gained the ability to run JavaScript plugins like this! I'll write more about that soon.)

Since it works with Datasette Lite, the live demo in the README now links to this demo on Datasette Lite.

entries.content:
13th November 2026

Release

datasette-cluster-map 0.19— Datasette plugin that shows a map for any data with latitude/longitude columns

One of the oldest Datasette plugins, and still one of my favorites. It now works with Datasette 1.0a42, and depends on the new datasette-leaflet to ensure OpenStreetMap tiles are requested with a referrer header.

Here's a map of power plants owned by California's PG&E, also demonstrating Datasette's recently redesigned facets:
